defaults.permitted_development: Across Surrey, change of use turns on the lawful existing use, the proposed use class and whether any specific permitted development route applies. In practice, frontage works, servicing, hours, noise and activity levels usually matter as much as the class label itself.

rules.height_rules: There is no automatic height allowance for change of use. Any new storey, plant, flue, lift overrun or rooftop equipment is separate operational development and needs its own assessment.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear additions, yards, seating areas, storage compounds or service bays are separate planning questions from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Surrey, the harder boundary issues are usually noise, servicing, odour, parking, deliveries, waste storage and the intensity of comings and goings near neighbouring occupiers.
rules.roof_rules: A use change does not automatically carry roof plant, vents, extraction kit or terraces with it. Those elements are assessed in their own right and can be the deciding issue for neighbours and design.
rules.materials_rules: Any external alterations such as shutters, signage, cladding, vents or changed openings should be judged as part of the wider street scene rather than as a minor afterthought to the use change.

rules.permitted_development: Change of use is not governed by a broad householder-style right. The starting point is the lawful existing use, the proposed class and any specific permitted route that genuinely applies. In Elmbridge, the hard planning question is often not the class move itself but whether the site can absorb the activity that comes with it.

rules.height_rules: Height is not the issue in the same way it is for householder work: any rooftop kit, extra bulk or new storey stands on its own planning footing. In Elmbridge, any new plant or roof bulk is usually judged against nearby housing rather than against the use-change principle itself.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear extensions, outdoor seating, storage yards, service bays or enlarged floorspace are separate planning issues from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: At the site edge, change of use cases are usually decided by activity and amenity rather than by measurements alone. In Elmbridge, the site edge is usually where intensified activity starts to show itself, through noise, vehicle movement and loss of privacy.
rules.roof_rules: New extract systems, vents, condensers, plant screens or roof terraces are not covered just because the use changes. They need their own planning assessment and can be decisive for neighbours.
rules.materials_rules: External alterations such as shopfront changes, shutters, signage, cladding or new openings are assessed separately and should fit the host building and the wider street scene. The planning question is usually less about the label of the use and more about traffic, amenity, servicing and the effect on the wider area.

restrictions.conservation_area: In a conservation area, the proposal is usually judged not only on use class but on whether the resulting frontage and activity respect the character of the place.
restrictions.listed_building: For a listed building, the use class analysis is only part of the answer. Any works affecting character usually need listed building consent.
restrictions.article4_notes: A specific Article 4 direction can still switch off the simpler change-of-use route for the exact property or area.
